name: What type of caulk is best for sealing bathroom trim and baseboards?

mainEntity.name: What type of caulk is best for sealing bathroom trim and baseboards?

acceptedAnswer.text: Bathroom carpentry trim requires high-quality, moisture-resistant acrylic latex caulk or hybrid polymer sealant with mildew-resistant additives. Bathrooms experience severe temperature swings and humidity cycles, causing walls and trim to expand and contract. Standard painter's caulk often cracks or develops mildew under these conditions. Finish carpenters apply flexible, paintable sealants along baseboard tops, vanity edges, and backsplash junctures to block steam from getting behind drywall while maintaining clean, smooth visual lines ready for interior paint.
acceptedAnswer.description: Use flexible, paintable acrylic latex or hybrid sealants formulated with mildew resistance to accommodate moisture and temperature shifts without cracking.
